title: webdav: nextcloud: rclone incorrectly retries long server-side chunks merge operations before they complete
body:
#### What is the problem you are having with rclone?

Uploading very large files (e.g. 20 GB) always fails because rclone keeps restarting the transfer while the server is still under the process of merging the chunks together.


#### What is your rclone version?
```
❯ rclone --version
rclone v1.63.0
- os/version: darwin 13.3.1 (64 bit)
- os/kernel: 22.4.0 (arm64)
- os/type: darwin
- os/arch: arm64 (ARMv8 compatible)
- go/version: go1.20.5
- go/linking: dynamic
- go/tags: none
```


#### Which OS you are using and how many bits?

```
❯ neofetch

                 ,xNMM.          --------------
               .OMMMMo           OS: macOS 13.3.1 22E261 arm64
               OMMM0,            Host: MacBookAir10,1

    kMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMMd     GPU: Apple M1
     ;KMMMMMMMWXXWMMMMMMMk.      Memory: 2991MiB / 16384MiB
       .cooc,.    .,coo:.
```


#### Which cloud storage system are you using?

WebDAV (NextCloud)


#### The command you were trying to run?

```
rclone copy verybigfile.bin nextcloud:
```


#### A log from the command with the `-vv` flag

My NextCloud instance is running out of storage so unfortunately I'm not able to provide such a log. It has been a long-standing issue though.

@participant2 I remember looking into it a very long time ago.
- For long operations, the HTTP `MOVE` request for merging chunks eventually times out (but the merge is actually still in progress).
- When trying to merge again then NextCloud returns a `LOCKED` error which I [tried to ignore](https://github.com/rclone/rclone/blob/2234feb23d1f9c50e94ad1c5b2d854282748cc03/backend/webdav/chunking.go#L30-L33).
- `rclone` seems to somehow figure out that the file isn't actually there, deletes the chunks, reuploads them, and tries to merge them again.
- Rinse and repeat.

There is [no API to check whether the `MOVE` operation is still in progress or not](https://github.com/nextcloud/server/issues/28395). The only way I know of is to check if it's still in progress is to [retry the `MOVE` until we don't receive a `LOCKED` error any longer](https://github.com/rclone/rclone/pull/6133#issuecomment-1184336893).

If I recall correctly, this workaround didn't work out: rclone eventually restarted the transfer anyway. Maybe rclone has some kind of mechanism to force retry "staled" transfers even if the backend asks it to wait?

👉 Would there be a way to work around this NextCloud limitation?

comments.body:
I think a loop is better than _--low-level-retries_.
Additionally, I suggest adding a new option/flag **nextcloud_merge_timeout** / **--nextcloud-merge-timeout**
Algorithm:
```
while elapsed_time < nextcloud_merge_timeout :
time = randint(10,30)
sleep(time) // Sleep random time (10 ~ 30 seconds)
check_if ( destination_file_exists && filesize_is_correct ) then_break
endwhile;
```

comments.author: participant9
comments.body: For the record : 404 as success is dangerous. I'll try to fix this on nextcloud itself as I'm planning to add some reliable hashing mechanism. Note that since there's no reliable hash mechanism on nextcloud status code is the only thing that can guarantee a client that the file was properly uploaded. This kind of behavior is one of the many reasons why a file might silently be corrupted during the upload. For this reason I would strongly advise to enable this new behavior only if some sort of "I know what I'm doing" parameter is given.

comments.author: participant9
comments.body:
I checked the logs on the nextcloud side. I have a lot of `- Part XX: Error executing "UploadPart"` errors when it happens. XX is the number of the part and interestingly its mostly multiples of 5.
The error involved is a `408 Request Timeout` on the S3 PUT method. I guess the multipart upload for S3 backend is pushing a bit too hard for the actual backend.

I think that on the NC side there's something related to file locking preventing the "normal" failure of the upload, which is fortunate since it prevents the abortion of the upload altogether.

The real fix would be to implement retries on 408 on the NC's S3 backend handler or some simultaneous part upload limiting configuration.

EDIT : follow up on investigation. It seems that the problem is located on the AWS sdk used by NC. There is a default retry per chunk but  maybe the conditions are too wild for 3 retries (the default value) to succeed. I'm reaching out to my S3 provider to see if there's any limitation on the bucket usage that could help pinpointing the problematic part.

comments.author: participant9
comments.body: @participant2 This needs to be reverted. The fix has to happen on Nextcloud. 423 + 404 is likely to happen if the multipart upload fails on NC and the abortMultipartUpload cleanup method is called. It gives too much room for a silently missing file. Please at least don't make if the default behavior.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
@participant9 I agree that is a horrible work around! However it does seem to fix things for users.

The workaround only kicks in if

1. We had a 423 error
2. We subsequently get a 404 error

How likely is it that this happens when it shouldn't? Have you actually seen it happen?

If the workaround does kick when it shouldn't then rclone will check the uploaded file to see it is the correct length and if not, upload it again.
